faqs.q: What are Enerpac adapters and what do they connect?
faqs.a: Enerpac adapters are small threaded fittings that change the port or thread of an Enerpac hydraulic hose, gauge or tool, such as an O-ring adapter, a thread-to-NPT adapter or a BSP male adapter. Five part numbers are listed, and each changes one thread to another.

faqs.q: What do the Enerpac adapter part numbers VSA444, FZ2069 and BA15025BSPM identify?
faqs.a: VSA444 is an adapter, FZ2007 is an O-ring adapter, FZ2056 is an adapter to NPT, FZ2069 is an SAE #8 to 3/8 inch NPT adapter and BA15025BSPM is a 1/4 inch BSP male adapter rated 1500 bar. Quote the number exactly when you order.

faqs.q: Which Enerpac adapter converts SAE #8 to 3/8 inch NPT?
faqs.a: FZ2069 is the Enerpac adapter listed as SAE #8 to 3/8 inch NPT. It is one of the five part numbers, alongside VSA444, FZ2007, FZ2056 and BA15025BSPM. Check both threads on your hose and tool before ordering.

faqs.q: How do I choose between the five Enerpac adapters VSA444, FZ2007, FZ2056, FZ2069 and BA15025BSPM?
faqs.a: Choose by the two threads to be joined. FZ2007 is an O-ring adapter, FZ2056 goes to NPT, FZ2069 goes from SAE #8 to 3/8 inch NPT, and BA15025BSPM has a 1/4 inch BSP male thread. VSA444 is listed as a plain adapter, so quote it with its threads.

faqs.q: What pressure rating do Enerpac adapters have?
faqs.a: BA15025BSPM is listed as a 1/4 inch BSP male adapter for 1500 bar. The other four part numbers do not carry a rating on this listing, so give us the working pressure and we will confirm the rating for the part before supply.

faqs.q: What material are Enerpac adapters made from?
faqs.a: The listing does not state the material of the five Enerpac adapters. Hydraulic tool adapters at this pressure are normally steel, but quote the part number and we will confirm the material with the manufacturer before you order.

faqs.q: Which thread standards do the Enerpac adapters cover?
faqs.a: The five part numbers cover SAE O-ring (SAE #8), NPT and BSP male threads. NPT is a tapered pipe thread and BSP male is the British pipe thread, so check which thread your equipment has, because NPT and BSP do not seal on each other.

faqs.q: What equipment do Enerpac adapters connect to?
faqs.a: They connect an Enerpac hose, coupler, gauge or cylinder port to a different thread, for example an SAE #8 port to a 3/8 inch NPT line. For the hydraulic power unit side see [hydraulic power unit components](/blog/hydraulic-power-unit-components).

faqs.q: How do I fit an Enerpac adapter safely?
faqs.a: Match both threads, seal the tapered NPT or BSP thread with a suitable sealant, and tighten to the thread's torque without over-tightening. Never use a pressure adapter on a line above its rating, especially a 1500 bar line.

faqs.q: How do Enerpac adapters differ from the Lube pump and motor adapters?
faqs.a: Enerpac adapters change the thread on a hydraulic tool line and are small threaded fittings. The [Lube pump/motor adapters](/p/lube-pump-motor-adapters) are cast aluminium mounting adapters that bolt a pump to a motor.

faqs.q: Are the Enerpac adapters genuine Enerpac parts?
faqs.a: The listing is for Enerpac-brand adapters under the Enerpac part numbers VSA444, FZ2007, FZ2056, FZ2069 and BA15025BSPM. Quote the part number and we confirm the item before supply, and ship worldwide from Dubai, UAE.

faqs.q: How do I read the Lovejoy collar part numbers 68514440122 and 68514440293?
faqs.a: Each long number is a Lovejoy stock number tied to a size: 68514440122 is the C226 collar, 68514440123 the C276, 68514440124 the C280, 68514440292 the C285 and 68514440293 the C295 and C2955 collar. Quote the size code and the stock number together.

faqs.q: Which Lovejoy C Type collar size do I need?
faqs.a: Match the size code stamped on your existing C Type hub or collar: C226, C276, C280, C285 or C295 (the C295 and C2955 share one part number). Sizes are not interchangeable, so quote the code from the old part.

faqs.q: What is the largest Lovejoy C Type collar on this listing?
faqs.a: The largest listed is the C295 and C2955 collar, sold under one part number, 68514440293. The smallest is the C226. Five sizes in all are listed, each with its hardware.

faqs.q: What torque or load rating do Lovejoy C Type collars have?

faqs.q: What material are Lovejoy C Type collars made from?

faqs.q: What standard do Lovejoy C Type collars follow?

faqs.q: What does a Lovejoy C Type collar connect to?

faqs.q: How do I fit a Lovejoy C Type collar?
faqs.a: Fit the collar and its hardware on the matching hub as the Lovejoy instructions for the size show, and tighten the hardware evenly. Replace worn collars in pairs with the matching spider, because a worn coupling damages the pump shaft.

faqs.q: How do Lovejoy C Type collars differ from the LC Type collars with screws?

faqs.q: What are Lovejoy L-Type jaw coupling hubs used for?
faqs.a: Lovejoy L-Type jaw coupling hubs are the shaft hubs of a jaw coupling, joining a pump shaft to a motor or engine shaft through a spider. 17 part numbers cover the L090, L095, L099 and L100 series in hub bores from 1/2" to 1-1/8", plus matching spiders.

faqs.q: How do I read the Lovejoy L-Type part numbers such as L095-1-1/8 and L090-5/8?
faqs.a: The first part is the series, L090, L095, L099 or L100, and the second part is the hub bore in inches: L095-1-1/8 is a 1-1/8 inch bore hub in the L095 series. Spiders are listed separately as the black solid centre and blue open centre.

faqs.q: Which bore sizes does each Lovejoy L-Type series offer?
faqs.a: L090 comes in 1/2", 5/8", 3/4" and 1". L095 comes in 1/2", 5/8", 3/4", 7/8", 1" and 1-1/8". L099 comes in 5/8" and 3/4", and L100 in 1" and 1-1/8". Match both shaft sizes before you order.

faqs.q: Which spider goes with the Lovejoy L090, L095, L099 and L100 hubs?
faqs.a: The L090 and L095 hubs take the black solid centre spider or the blue open centre spider, and the L099 and L100 hubs take the blue open centre spider. Use a spider of the same series with each hub pair.

faqs.q: What torque rating do the Lovejoy L-Type jaw coupling hubs have?
faqs.a: The listing gives no torque figure, so check the Lovejoy rating for the series and the application. Quote the motor power, speed and shaft sizes and we will confirm the series with the manufacturer before supply.

faqs.q: What are Lovejoy L-Type hubs and spiders made from?
faqs.a: The listing does not name the hub material. The spider is the flexible element between the jaws and is a wear part, listed as a hydraulic spider with a solid or open centre. Quote the part number and we confirm material details.

faqs.q: What does a Lovejoy L-Type jaw coupling hub connect to?
faqs.a: One hub goes on the pump shaft and the other on the motor or engine shaft, with the spider between them. The pump is mounted with a bell housing or bracket, such as the [Magnaloy pump mounting brackets and bell housings](/p/magnaloy-pump-mounting-brackets-and-bell-housings).

faqs.q: How do I replace the spider in a Lovejoy L-Type jaw coupling?
faqs.a: Move the pump or motor back, take out the old spider, fit a new one of the same series between the hub jaws and slide the units together. Replace a spider that is cracked, hardened or worn thin, since it is the wear part of the coupling.

faqs.q: Where are Lovejoy L-Type jaw couplings used on power units?
faqs.a: They join the electric motor to the pump in hydraulic power units, where the pump flange and motor frame set the alignment. See [hydraulic power unit components](/blog/hydraulic-power-unit-components) for how the motor, coupling and pump fit together.

faqs.q: How do I read the Lovejoy LC collar part numbers such as 68514447932 and 68514448340?

faqs.q: Which Lovejoy LC collar size matches my coupling?

faqs.q: Do the Lovejoy LC090 and LC095 collars share a part number?

faqs.q: What torque rating do Lovejoy LC collars have?

faqs.q: What material are Lovejoy LC collars made from?

faqs.q: What standard do Lovejoy LC Type collars follow?

faqs.q: What are Lube pump/motor adapters and what do they do?
faqs.a: Lube pump/motor adapters are cast aluminium adapters that bolt a hydraulic pump to an electric motor, with an access hole for easy coupling adjustment. Ten part numbers cover SAE A, B and C pump mounts on 56C to 405TC motor frames.

faqs.q: How do I read the Lube pump/motor adapter numbers such as 6027, 1983 and 6029?
faqs.a: Each number names a pump mount and a motor frame range. 6027 is SAE AA on 56C to 145TC frames, 6034 is SAE A on 182 to 256TC, 1951 is SAE B on 182TC to 256TC, 1983 is SAE C on 324 to 405TC, and 6029 is a 4F17 pump flange on 56C to 145TC.

faqs.q: Which Lube pump/motor adapter fits an SAE B pump on a 182TC to 256TC motor?
faqs.a: Parts 1951 and 1952 are listed as SAE B on 182TC to 256TC frames. SAE A on the same frames is 1950, 1959 and 1960 (and 6034 for 182 to 256). Match both the pump flange and the motor frame size.

faqs.q: Which Lube adapter fits an SAE C pump?
faqs.a: Part 1983 is the SAE C pump/motor adapter, for 324 to 405TC motor frames. It is the only SAE C part on the listing, which also carries SAE AA, A and B parts and a 4F17 flange.

faqs.q: What pressure or torque rating do Lube pump/motor adapters have?
faqs.a: The listing gives no pressure or torque rating: an adapter carries the pump and motor alignment, not fluid pressure. The coupling and pump set the torque limit, so quote the motor power and pump model if you need a check.

faqs.q: What are Lube pump/motor adapters made from?
faqs.a: They are cast aluminium with a plain finish. Aluminium keeps the unit light and dissipates heat, and the access hole in the casting lets you adjust the coupling without taking the pump off.

faqs.q: Which SAE pump mounts do Lube pump/motor adapters match?
faqs.a: The ten part numbers cover SAE AA, A, B and C pump flanges, plus a 4F17 flange on 56C to 145TC motors. The SAE A 2-bolt pattern is the common small pump mount, while SAE C is for larger pumps.

faqs.q: What does a Lube pump/motor adapter connect?
faqs.a: It joins an electric motor frame, such as 56C to 145TC, to a hydraulic pump with a matching SAE flange, with a coupling inside it. For the coupling hubs see the [Lovejoy L-Type jaw coupling hubs](/p/lovejoy-l-type-jaw-coupling-hubs).

faqs.q: How do I set the coupling through the access hole in a Lube pump/motor adapter?
faqs.a: Bolt the adapter to the motor, fit the coupling halves on the shafts and use the access hole to set the gap and tighten the set screws. Then bolt the pump to the adapter. Mounting is horizontal or vertical.

The [Magnaloy pump mounting brackets and bell housings](/p/magnaloy-pump-mounting-brackets-and-bell-housings) are brackets for pump and engine mounts, in seven part numbers.

faqs.q: What are Lube return flanges and what do they do?
faqs.a: Lube return flanges are steel flanges that bolt on a hydraulic reservoir to take a return line, in four pipe sizes from 3/4" to 1-1/2". They come with mounting hardware: two 1/4-20 thread-forming screws, and a neoprene rubber washer.

faqs.q: How do the Lube return flange part numbers 5111 to 5114 map to pipe sizes?
faqs.a: The numbers rise with the pipe size: 5111 is for 3/4 inch pipe, 5112 for 1 inch, 5113 for 1-1/4 inch and 5114 for 1-1/2 inch. Quote the number or the pipe size when you order.

faqs.q: Which Lube return flange do I need for 1 inch pipe?
faqs.a: Part 5112 is the Lube return flange for 1 inch pipe. It is supplied in hydraulic steel with two 1/4-20 thread-forming screws and a neoprene rubber washer, so no extra mounting hardware is needed.

faqs.q: What sizes of Lube return flange are available?
faqs.a: Four sizes are listed: 3/4 inch (5111), 1 inch (5112), 1-1/4 inch (5113) and 1-1/2 inch (5114). They are return flanges, so they suit the return line, not the suction side.

faqs.q: What pressure rating do Lube return flanges have?
faqs.a: The listing gives no pressure rating, and a return flange sits on a low-pressure tank line. Quote your line pressure and we will confirm the suitability of the part before supply.

faqs.q: What are Lube return flanges and their washers made from?
faqs.a: The listing gives hydraulic steel for the flange and neoprene rubber for the washer. Neoprene resists mineral oil and gives a seal between the flange and the tank wall.

faqs.q: Which thread and pipe standards apply to Lube return flanges?
faqs.a: The flanges are sold by pipe size, 3/4 inch to 1 1/2 inch, and are fixed with 1/4-20 thread-forming screws. The listing names no further standard, so quote the pipe size and the tank wall thickness if you need a check.

faqs.q: What does a Lube return flange mount on?
faqs.a: It mounts on the wall of a hydraulic reservoir with the two included screws and takes the return pipe of the size stated. For the suction side see the [Lube suction flanges](/p/lube-suction-flanges).

faqs.q: How do I install a Lube return flange on a reservoir?
faqs.a: Drill the tank wall to the pipe size, fit the neoprene washer between the flange and the tank and drive the two 1/4-20 thread-forming screws. Check for leaks after filling and warming the oil.

faqs.q: How do Lube return flanges differ from the Lube suction flanges?
faqs.a: Return flanges are listed for return lines in four sizes from 3/4" to 1-1/2" with two screws and a neoprene washer. The [suction flanges](/p/lube-suction-flanges) are listed in five sizes up to 2 inch and come with four thread-forming screws.

faqs.q: What are Lube suction flanges and what do they do?
faqs.a: Lube suction flanges are hydraulic steel flanges that bolt on a reservoir to take the pump suction line. Five pipe sizes run from 3/4 inch to 2 inch, and each comes with mounting hardware: four 5/16-18 thread-forming screws.

faqs.q: How do the Lube suction flange part numbers 5101 to 5105 map to pipe sizes?
faqs.a: The numbers rise with the size: 5101 is for 3/4 inch pipe, 5102 for 1 inch, 5103 for 1 1/4 inch, 5104 for 1.5 inch and 5105 for 2 inch. Quote the number or the pipe size when you order.

faqs.q: Which Lube suction flange do I need for 2 inch pipe?
faqs.a: Part 5105 is the Lube suction flange for 2 inch pipe, the largest size. It is hydraulic steel and comes with four 5/16-18 thread-forming screws.

faqs.q: How many sizes of Lube suction flange are available?
faqs.a: Five: 3/4 inch (5101), 1 inch (5102), 1 1/4 inch (5103), 1.5 inch (5104) and 2 inch (5105). Pick the size to match the suction pipe, and remember the suction line should not be smaller than the pump inlet.

faqs.q: What pressure rating do Lube suction flanges have?
faqs.a: The listing gives no pressure rating. A suction flange works at tank or slightly negative pressure, not system pressure. Quote the application and we will confirm the part before supply.

faqs.q: What are Lube suction flanges made from?
faqs.a: The listing gives hydraulic steel, supplied with its screws as mounting hardware. Check the seal or gasket between the flange and the tank wall at fitting.

faqs.q: Which thread and pipe standards apply to Lube suction flanges?
faqs.a: The flanges are sold by pipe size, 3/4 inch to 2 inch, and fixed with 5/16-18 thread-forming screws. The listing names no further standard, so quote the pipe size and the tank wall thickness if you need a check.

faqs.q: What does a Lube suction flange mount on?
faqs.a: It mounts on a hydraulic reservoir and takes the suction pipe of the size stated, with four 5/16-18 screws. For the tank return side see the [Lube return flanges](/p/lube-return-flanges).

faqs.q: How do I fit a Lube suction flange to a reservoir?
faqs.a: Drill the tank to the pipe size, seat the flange with a sealing washer or gasket and drive the four thread-forming screws evenly. Check that no air can enter, because a suction leak makes the pump noisy and foams the oil.

faqs.q: How do Lube suction flanges differ from the Lube return flanges?
faqs.a: Suction flanges come in five sizes up to 2 inch with four 5/16-18 screws, while the [return flanges](/p/lube-return-flanges) come in four smaller sizes with two screws and a neoprene washer.

faqs.q: What are Magnaloy pump mounting brackets and bell housings used for?
faqs.a: They mount a hydraulic pump to an engine or electric motor so the shafts line up. Seven part numbers are listed, including a 4-bolt pump mounting bracket and several pump/engine mounts such as E575502A and E575522A.

faqs.q: How do I read the Magnaloy part numbers 3030, 3032 and E575502A?
faqs.a: 3030 is a 4-bolt pump mounting bracket, 3032 is a hydraulic pump mounting bracket, and the E5755 and E5756 numbers are pump/engine mounts. The AA suffix, as in E575502AA, is a variant of the E575502A mount, so quote the exact code.

faqs.q: Which Magnaloy part is the 4-bolt pump mounting bracket?
faqs.a: 3030 is the 4-bolt pump mounting bracket. 3032 is a hydraulic pump mounting bracket under its own number, and the other five parts are pump/engine mounts.

faqs.q: How do I choose between the Magnaloy pump/engine mounts E575502A, E575522A and E575602A?
faqs.a: Match the engine and the pump flange you are using, because each number is a different mount. The AA variants, E575502AA and E575522AA, sit alongside the A versions, so quote the complete code from your old mount.

faqs.q: What torque or load rating do Magnaloy pump mounts have?
faqs.a: The listing gives no rating. Pump mounts carry the pump and keep the shafts aligned, so the limit is the pump and engine, not the bracket. Quote the pump model and engine and we check fit before supply.

faqs.q: What are Magnaloy pump mounting brackets made from?
faqs.a: The listing does not state the material of the brackets and bell housings. Quote the part number and we confirm the material before supply.

faqs.q: What mounting standard do Magnaloy pump brackets follow?
faqs.a: The listing does not name a mounting standard. Each bracket or pump/engine mount is identified by its part number, such as 3030 or E575502A, so quote the pump flange and the engine so we confirm the match before supply.

faqs.q: What does a Magnaloy pump mounting bracket connect?
faqs.a: It joins a hydraulic pump to an engine or motor, with the coupling between them. For the coupling hubs see the [Lovejoy L-Type jaw coupling hubs](/p/lovejoy-l-type-jaw-coupling-hubs), and for a cast aluminium motor adapter see [Lube pump/motor adapters](/p/lube-pump-motor-adapters).

faqs.q: How do I align a pump on a Magnaloy bracket?
faqs.a: Bolt the bracket to the engine or motor, fit the coupling halves, mount the pump and check the shafts for runout and gap. A misaligned coupling wears the spider and the pump shaft seal. See [hydraulic power unit components](/blog/hydraulic-power-unit-components).

faqs.q: How do Magnaloy brackets differ from Lube pump/motor adapters?
faqs.a: The Magnaloy parts are brackets and pump/engine mounts in seven part numbers, while the [Lube pump/motor adapters](/p/lube-pump-motor-adapters) are cast aluminium adapters in ten part numbers that tie an SAE pump flange to a motor frame.
